basics.name: Chencheng Li
basics.label: UC San Diego CS | Software Engineering & Applied AI | Co-founder, JGP E-commerce
basics.summary:
I’m a computer science undergraduate at UC San Diego, expecting to graduate in December 2026. My background combines software engineering, AI research, business operations, and entrepreneurship.
I build practical tools with Python, SQL, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, React, and TypeScript. In Agent OS, I integrated Amazon operations data and developed data-quality checks and decision-support tools. My coursework covers data structures, algorithms, databases, scalable analytics, computer vision, and deep learning. I implemented configurable ResNet models in PyTorch and contributed an IndexedDB data layer to a team software project.
In UCSD’s Early Research Scholars Program, I developed Blender APIs and worked on model evaluation. I now tutor CSE110 Software Engineering.
Co-founding an e-commerce business and working in industry gave me experience communicating with customers, coordinating across teams, and connecting technical implementation with real business needs.

work.name: UC San Diego
work.position: Undergraduate Researcher | Early Research Scholars Program

projects.name: Agent OS
highlights: Built an Amazon operations backend with Python, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL, bringing together order, inventory, advertising, fee, and product data from four stores in a React/Next.js dashboard.
Added freshness and missing-input checks, source tracking, and decision traces to surface evidence gaps before execution.
Developed inventory-aware advertising anomaly detection, issue deduplication, and replenishment recommendations with explicit constraints and validation.

projects.name: Configurable ResNet Models in PyTorch
highlights: Implemented configurable ResNet models in PyTorch, enabling per-block BatchNorm/Dynamic Tanh substitutions and ablation studies across ResNet-18 and ResNet-50.

projects.name: TritonCard
highlights: Implemented an IndexedDB data layer for a team project, including card definitions, player collections, asynchronous JSON loading, and APIs to add, remove, and query collection items.
Improved shared initialization, local and GitHub Pages asset-path handling, and the collection page’s responsive layout and game integration.

projects.name: LLM Decision-Making Evaluation
highlights: Evaluated 20 operations-reasoning problems under three input conditions, with three repetitions per condition and 180 recorded final answers.
Examined model outputs and reference answers separately, using independent scoring and task-clustered analysis to compare results.
